case: NLRB v. Town & Country Electric, Inc.
disposition: Reverse the Eighth Circuit categorical employee-exclusion ruling and remand, 9–0, reserving other liability, individual coverage and remedy questions.
disposition_summary: Reverse the Eighth Circuit categorical employee-exclusion ruling and remand, 9–0, reserving other liability, individual coverage and remedy questions.

judgments.disposition: Reverse the Eighth Circuit categorical employee-exclusion ruling and remand, 9–0, reserving other liability, individual coverage and remedy questions.

law_summary: Union compensation and compatible organizing obligations do not categorically exclude a worker or applicant from NLRA employee status. The Board's actual inclusion is permissible within the statute and common-law service principles; neither mandatory coverage of every organizer nor misconduct immunity is established. Existing exclusions, actual control, qualifications, liability and individual remedy requirements continue to govern.
next_stage: Remand to the Eighth Circuit for proper consideration of remaining grounds, with any appropriate Board or compliance proceedings; no automatic award or further Supreme Court event is set.
